content: 1. Spinosad is a dermatological agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of head lice infestations. 2. Common adverse reactions include redness at the application site and redness in the eyes. 3. Spinosad Topical Suspension is indicated for the topical treatment of head lice infestations in patients aged 4 years and older. 4. It should be used as part of a comprehensive lice management program, which includes washing recently worn clothing, hats, bedding, and towels in hot water or dry-cleaning them. 5. Personal care items such as combs, brushes, and hair clips should also be washed in hot water. 6. A fine-tooth comb or special nit comb may be used to remove dead lice and nits. 7. Spinosad Topical Suspension is for topical use only and is not intended for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use. 8. Shake the bottle well before use. Apply enough suspension to cover the dry scalp and then apply to dry hair. 9. Depending on hair length, up to 120 mL (one bottle) may be required to adequately cover the scalp and hair. 10. Leave the suspension on for 10 minutes, then rinse thoroughly with warm water. 11. If live lice are observed 7 days after the first treatment, a second treatment should be applied. 12. Avoid contact with the eyes. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. 13. Spinosad contains benzyl alcohol and is not recommended for use in neonates and infants under 6 months of age due to the risk of serious adverse reactions and death associated with systemic exposure to benzyl alcohol. 14. Clinical trials have shown that Spinosad Topical Suspension is effective in treating head lice infestations, with safety and efficacy established in pediatric patients aged 4 years and older. 15. Safety in pediatric patients under 4 years of age has not been established, and it is not recommended for use in children under 6 months of age due to the potential for increased systemic absorption and immature skin barriers. 16. Spinosad works by causing neuronal excitation in insects, leading to paralysis and death after periods of hyperexcitation. 17. Spinosad is derived from the fermentation of a soil bacterium, Saccharopolyspora spinosa, and is a mixture of spinosyn A and spinosyn D in a 5:1 ratio. 18. The topical suspension contains 9 mg of Spinosad per gram in a viscous, slightly opaque, light orange-colored vehicle. 19. Spinosad has not been studied for pharmacodynamics, and systemic absorption in humans is minimal, as demonstrated by plasma levels below the limit of quantification in clinical studies. 20. Spinosad has shown no evidence of mutagenic or clastogenic potential in genotoxicity tests and no effects on growth, fertility, or reproduction in animal studies at doses up to 10 mg/kg/day. 21. Pregnant women should use Spinosad only if clearly needed, as there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies have shown no teratogenic effects, but maternal toxicity was observed at high doses. 22. Nursing mothers should exercise caution when using Spinosad, as it contains benzyl alcohol, which may be systemically absorbed through the skin. The amount excreted in human milk is unknown. 23. Lactating women may choose to pump and discard breast milk for 8 hours after use to avoid infant ingestion of benzyl alcohol. 24. Spinosad is not recommended for use in geriatric patients due to insufficient data on responses in individuals aged 65 and older. 25. There is no FDA guidance on the use of Spinosad in specific populations, including those with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients, or specific gender or racial groups. 26. If oral ingestion occurs, medical advice should be sought immediately. 27. Spinosad Topical Suspension should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with excursions permitted between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). 28. Patients should be instructed to shake the bottle well before use, apply the suspension only to dry scalp and hair, avoid swallowing, and wash hands after application. 29. Spinosad should only be used on children under the direct supervision of an adult. 30. If pregnant or breastfeeding, patients should consult a physician before use. 31. Spinosad is supplied in 120 mL bottles and should be kept out of reach of children. 32. There is no established interaction between Spinosad and alcohol, but patients should consult their doctor regarding potential effects. 33. Spinosad is marketed under the brand name SPINOSAD®. 34. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for Spinosad.
